confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on two web searches of cost-of-living aggregators, including Numbeo data as of June 2026 and mid-2026 updates from other sources. Beer, coffee and the inexpensive meal are reasonably well supported. Sources agree on a cappuccino at about $5.50–7.70 and an inexpensive meal at about $20–24. For draft beer, most sources put it at about $7–9.70. Expat Arrivals lists $3.50 for a local draft, which looks too low, so I left it out. The mid-range meal for two is less certain because sources range from $80 to $118, and I used about $100. I didn't search cocktail or wine prices directly. I estimated them from how they usually compare to beer in US cities and from general knowledge of Denver bars, so they are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are general model estimates for Denver in July, which is peak summer season. I didn't look at any live booking pages or current listings. Denver has few hostels, so the hostel figures are especially uncertain.
comparable_city_reasoning: Denver is priced as a fairly expensive mid-to-large US city. It sits above the US average but below New York and San Francisco, roughly in line with Austin and Portland. Summer is high season for tourism and conventions.
